title: Black Oak: Ancient Black Oaks You Can Visit
meta_description: An eastern North American oak. Two in East Flatbush, Brooklyn, are believed to be the last of a wood cut down in the 1940s.
intro: The black oak is an oak of eastern North America, and we map it in four cities. The two in East Flatbush, Brooklyn, stand on sidewalks 240 metres apart, and NYC Parks believes they are survivors of the Paerdegat Woods, cleared in the 1940s, though no survey has dated either trunk. New York's Woodlawn Cemetery kept another when it laid out its grounds, and Parks puts it at nearly 300 years. Cleveland's Lake View Cemetery counts its black oak among the trees surveyors in 1946 believed were standing before 1796, and now holds it together with cables and brace rods. The Cook County champion at Willow Springs Woods outside Chicago is the only one with a measured height, 36.6 metres on a crown barely 14 across. At the Arnold Arboretum in Boston grows a clone, grafted in 1883 from a tree George Engelmann described, and nobody knows which.
